description:
The crate-level Features doc at lib.rs:100-111 enumerates what the
`serde` feature adds:

> Adds `serde::Serialize` and `serde::Deserialize` derives to
> [`Error`] and [`IoFailure`], and propagates `pkix-path/serde` so
> the re-exported [`DerError`] gains the matching wire form.

That description is incomplete. Enabling `pkix-truststore/serde`
propagates `pkix-path/serde`, which also adds `Serialize/Deserialize`
to the re-exported [`TrustAnchor`] (pkix-path/src/lib.rs:649):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct TrustAnchor { ... }
```

A caller reading pkix-truststore's docs would conclude only the error
types and `DerError` gain serde behavior, and miss that `Vec<TrustAnchor>`
is also serializable. The canonical caller use case for the `serde`
feature is exactly the inverse of what the doc emphasizes: callers turn
it on to **cache parsed trust stores** (e.g., load 200 anchors once at
startup, serialize the Vec to a cache file, reload on warm-start without
re-parsing PEM). That use case is invisible from the current doc.

This is a docs-as-contract gap: an undocumented capability that callers
benefit from depends on a feature flag whose docs do not mention the
capability.

Fix: extend the bullet to enumerate all types that gain serde behavior
via the propagation. Suggested text:

```
//! - **`serde`** (off by default) — adds `serde::Serialize` and
//!   `serde::Deserialize` derives to [`Error`] and [`IoFailure`], and
//!   propagates `pkix-path/serde` so the re-exported [`TrustAnchor`]
//!   and [`DerError`] gain matching wire forms. The canonical use is
//!   caching: load anchors once with `from_pem_file`, serialize the
//!   resulting `Vec<TrustAnchor>` to a process-local cache, and on
//!   warm-start deserialize back instead of re-parsing PEM.
```

The `TrustAnchor` wire form uses pkix-path's `serde_der` module (base64
in human-readable serializers, raw bytes in binary), per
pkix-path/Cargo.toml:23. That detail belongs in pkix-path's own docs;
pkix-truststore only needs to acknowledge the surface exists.

Engineering basis: real caller use case (cache hydration) silently
supported. Not opinion — closing the gap between code behavior and
documented contract is a routine docs-fix.
title: serde feature docs omit TrustAnchor; rustdoc only mentions DerError gains serde via pkix-path/serde propagation
